To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

management of the implementation process of a web-based information systems must be seen as a continuous and ongoing process, where the management must be able to adapt to the changing needs of the users.

“The organizational context for implementing web-based information systems can be characterized as either a) a change management context, b) a change implementation context, c) a change adaptation context, or d) a change assimilation context.”

the management of a distributed organization must be prepared to handle the following four implementation contexts: 1) the management of the implementation context, 2) the implementation context for the implementation of the web-based information system, 3) the management of implementation contexts for the use of the web-based system, and 4) the implementation context of the use of the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the management of change and the management of knowledge, and we argue that the two issues are closely related.
the organizational and managerial aspects of implementing web-based information systems in distributed organizations.
the implementation of a web-based information systems in a large distributed organization with a focus on change management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the organizational implementation of web-based information systems is a complex and dynamic process.
the organizational context for change is a critical factor for the implementation of web-based information systems.
there are four different implementation contexts, each of which requires different management approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the implementation of web-based information systems is not a one-time event, but a continuous process that involves the organization as a whole and requires a change management approach.

the implementation of open-ended, configurable and context specific web- based information systems in a distributed organization is an improvisational process, where the organizational change management process can be characterized as a process of continuous learning and adaptation.
a web-based information systems implementation is not only a technological issue, but also a management issue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the implementation of web-based information systems can be characterized in a number of different ways.
change management for web-based information systems should not be seen as one, but rather as four different and general approaches.
a more holistic and context sensitive view on implementation and change is required.
